To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the translation, processing, and formation of poliovirus in a HeLa cell extract are optimal at 34 degrees, that the synthesis of poliovirus RNA is optimal at 30-34 degrees C, and that the synthesis of virus is inhibited at 36-38 degrees C.

poliovirus translation, proteolytical processing, and virus synthesis are more efficient at 33 degrees C than at higher or lower temperatures and that lipid synthesis is required for efficient in vitro translation and virus formation.

poliovirus formation is more efficient in HeLa cell extract at 34 degrees than at 30 and 36 degrees C, that lipid synthesis is required for poliovirus formation, and that the viral RNA polymerase is sensitive to lipid synthesis inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of lipophilic agents, temperature, and cell membranes on the in vitro translation, processing, and RNA synthesis of poliovirus.
the effects of temperature and lipids on translation, proteolyic processing, and viral RNA synthesis in a HeLa cell extract.
the effects of lipophilic compounds on poliovirus translation and RNA synthesis in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in vitro translation and processing are membrane dependent, whereas RNA polymerase synthesis is independent of membranes and is inhibited by oleic but not cerulenin.
the synthesis of poliovirus RNA in a cell-free translation extract is a complex process that requires a delicate balance of temperature, lipophilic agents, and membranes.
the in vitro translation and processing events are optimal at 34 degrees, whereas the in vitro RNA synthesis is optimal at 32 to 34 degrees C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in vitro translation and proteolytic processing of viral proteins require intact membranes.
poliovirus translation and protein processing are more efficient at 30 degrees C than at higher temperatures, whereas viral RNA synthesis is more efficient at higher temperatures.
the formation of poliovirus in vitro is temperature dependent, requires intact membranes, and is affected by lipophilic agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
poliovirus formation in vitro is highly temperature dependent.
the formation of virus in vitro requires the participation of intact membranes and that this requirement may be related to the requirement of lipid for the synthesis of viral RNA.

the in vitro translation, processing, and viral RNA synthesis systems in HeLa cell S-30 extracts are sensitive to temperature and to lipophilic agents, which may be useful in the study of poliovirus assembly.
